title: How do you answer "What is your biggest weakness?" honestly and well?
description: How to answer the weakness question in consulting interviews, with weak and strong example answers and how to show self-awareness.
hook: The weakness question is less about the weakness and more about self-awareness. Interviewers want someone who knows where they struggle and is actively doing something about it.
body:
The question

What is your biggest weakness?

A weak answer

I'm a perfectionist, so I sometimes spend too long making my work perfect.

Why it falls short: The most common answer of all. It sounds rehearsed and avoids admitting a real weakness.

A strong answer

I used to avoid giving direct feedback to colleagues, because I worried about upsetting them. In one project that meant a teammate kept making the same error in our analysis until it reached the client. Since then I've made it a habit to give feedback within a day, starting with what went well and then one specific thing to change. I asked my manager to check how I'm doing at my last review, and she said it had noticeably improved, though it still takes effort.

Why it works: A real weakness that matters at work, a concrete consequence, specific actions to improve and honest evidence of progress.

Make it your own

Copy the shape of the strong answer, not its words. Write your own version of "What is your biggest weakness?" in five or six sentences from a real moment, then say it aloud until it sounds natural.
